verdict.rationale: Zero says it does not track, collect, or sell user data, and it discloses that user emails are stored in a Durable Object and an R2 bucket. That gives thin support for the transparency half of the story, but nothing in the evidence shows blocking of tracking or read pixels, by default or otherwise. missing for 10: documented default blocking of tracking/read pixels, remote-image/sender-tracking protection controls, a detailed privacy policy or data-handling documentation (including AI processing of mail), independent or hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As a switcher, the client protects me from senders' tracking — blocking read pixels by default — and is transparent about what it does with my mail data

citations.quote: Zero does not track, collect, or sell your data in any way.
We're now storing the user's emails in their Durable Object & an R2 bucket.
